definition: One route = actual origin station to final destination station in one direction, without passenger transfer. Repeat departures are trips, not new routes. International routes belong to the origin country.
coverage: All 51 country editions have coverage and status notes, including Caucasus and transcontinental editions. Endpoint inventory remains partial: dated Renfe and SNCF data plus selected official published endpoints. Unresolved records are excluded, not counted as zero real-world services.

countries.name: Spain
countries.note: Dated Renfe first/last-stop extraction, 24–30 October 2026. Six foreign-origin services are attributed to France or Portugal rather than to Spain. Feed scope only; other Spanish operators remain incomplete.

countries.name: France
countries.note: Dated SNCF rail endpoints plus France-origin services from the Renfe feed, 24–30 October 2026, and selected published endpoints. Buses, tram-trains and shuttles excluded; other operators remain partial.

countries.name: Germany
countries.note: ICE/IC line maps show corridors and intermediate stops, not a complete list of train first/last stops. Imported endpoint services are partial.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.note: Operator/network maps are not terminal inventories. Confirmed international endpoints included; domestic train-level coverage remains incomplete.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.note: EuroCity Rotterdam–Brussels is distinct from Eurocity Direct, which can originate at Lelystad or Amsterdam Zuid. Intermediate Amsterdam pairs are not assumed full routes.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.note: IC 01 terminal pair imported; Brussels and Bruges are intermediate stops on that line. Other line patterns and short workings require more train-level evidence.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.note: Chur/Tirano and St. Moritz/Tirano are distinct full services. Dates and Vereina diversion must be respected; no blanket Glacier Express active-service claim.

countries.name: Italy
countries.note: Named long-distance services reviewed; city names alone do not verify exact terminal stations. Bernina international endpoint services admitted separately; domestic coverage remains incomplete.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.note: Direct timetable columns distinguish Cork endpoint trains from Tralee through trains. Transfer connections are not promoted.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.note: Copenhagen/Hamburg full services are distinct from longer Railjet services and from intermediate Odense pairs. Engineering changes can alter endpoints.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.note: Published Porto Campanhã/Faro AP terminals plus the Portugal-origin Porto–Vigo service in dated Renfe data. Lisbon is intermediate on the AP trains. Connecting journeys are excluded.

countries.name: Austria
countries.note: Vienna Westbahnhof is the published Dacia/Someș terminal; Budapest is intermediate. These few services are not an inventory of Austrian rail routes.

countries.name: Poland
countries.note: Warszawa Wschodnia/München Hbf published direct service imported. Whole-network PKP train-origin/terminus coverage remains incomplete.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.note: Published city pairs include both full services and Dacia through services. Exact dated origin stations during works remain unresolved; none promoted from generic Budapest city-pair facts.

countries.name: Romania
countries.note: București Nord/Wien Westbahnhof and Baia Mare/Wien Westbahnhof endpoints confirmed. Corrections during 27–29 October works require dated checking.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.note: Full international endpoint pair confirmed by the operator’s revised timetable notice. Other domestic city pairs lack full first/last-stop verification.

countries.name: Albania
countries.note: Current official passenger timetable could not be retrieved. No verified endpoint route is published here; this is not proof that no passenger train exists.

countries.name: Greece
countries.note: Athens/Thessaloniki full Intercity route confirmed; Larissa and Katerini not counted as new endpoints for that service.

countries.name: Türkiye
countries.note: Ankara/Halkalı endpoint service distinguished from the seasonal tourist Eastern Express. Sofia service uses Halkalı, not central Istanbul.

countries.name: Norway
countries.note: Trondheim S/Bodø daytime endpoints retained. The Nordland night service is suspended until at least January 2027; sleeper branding and overnight sample times removed. Other operators and routes remain incomplete.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.note: Berlin and Dresden endings are date-dependent. Friday services extending to Dresden are not also counted as Berlin-ending trips. SJ whole-network evidence remains incomplete.

countries.name: Finland
countries.note: Helsinki/Kemijärvi full journey confirmed. A stop at Rovaniemi does not create a second full endpoint service; broader VR trip-level coverage remains incomplete.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.note: Selected national corridors. Prague station endings vary by operator and engineering works; only independently evidenced full endpoints enter the direct list.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.note: Selected trunk corridors. TATRAN/KRIVÁŇ express-service notices and named international terminal publications are linked in the route list. Older IC marketing examples are not current IC frequency evidence. Exact dated operation remains to be checked.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.note: Selected railway corridors. Check replacement buses and works; a timetable connection containing a change is excluded from the full-train directory.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.note: Selected domestic corridors. Seasonal services and bus replacements require a dated check; Zagreb can be an intermediate stop on an Osijek–Split train.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina

source.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina · official railway / transport reference

countries.note: Separate operator networks. Selected ŽFBH full endpoints are listed; Republika Srpska corridors are mapped but their full endpoint inventory is unresolved. Check restoration notices and operating days.

countries.name: Serbia
countries.note: Selected corridors only. Novi Sad station access and route endpoints have changed; use the operator’s current timetable, not a city-pair assumption.

countries.name: Montenegro
countries.note: Bar–Bijelo Polje regional trains and Podgorica–Nikšić have distinct full endpoints. International trains continue into Serbia; intermediate Podgorica pairs are excluded.

countries.name: Kosovo
countries.note: Selected Prishtinë–Pejë regional corridor. Published operator timetable is labelled 2025; current operating days require reconfirmation. No international connection is implied. Kosovo is shown as a separate atlas edition without a position on recognition.

countries.name: North Macedonia

source.name: North Macedonia · official railway / transport reference

countries.note: Selected domestic corridors and published full endpoints. Train 641 continues beyond Bitola to Žabeni, so its Bitola stop is not counted as a terminus; trains 643/645 end at Bitola. Check current disruptions. No international service to Greece or Serbia is implied.

countries.name: Luxembourg
countries.note: Selected CFL trunk corridors and the Kautenbach–Wiltz regional shuttle. Most corridor names do not establish full train terminals: through trains and short workings must be checked individually. Check current works and reduced service. Coverage remains partial.

countries.name: Estonia
countries.note: Selected intercity and regional corridors. Tallinn–Vilnius itineraries may involve a change and are not counted as a single direct route.

countries.name: Latvia
countries.note: Selected mainline corridors. Transfer icons in operator timetables mean separate trains and are not promoted to full endpoint journeys.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.note: Selected domestic corridors. October/November engineering timetables supersede annual sheets. Nida and Palanga extensions are buses, not direct railway routes.

countries.name: Moldova
countries.note: Selected Prietenia international corridor. Border procedures and time zones affect duration. No service to Odesa or through Transnistria is implied.

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.note: Selected published international full-train services. Connections shown after a transfer at Przemyśl or Chełm remain separate routes. Disruptions can alter dates and endpoints.

countries.name: Belarus
countries.note: Selected domestic corridors. Cross-border availability is not inferred from infrastructure; check current operator restrictions.

countries.name: Russia
countries.note: European trunk corridors only, not the entire Russian network. Sapsan full terminals are listed; other corridors require separate train-level evidence.

countries.name: Armenia
countries.note: Caucasus edition. Yerevan–Tbilisi and summer Yerevan–Batumi are distinct seasonal endpoints. No passenger border link to Azerbaijan or Türkiye is implied.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
countries.note: Caucasus edition. Selected domestic corridors only. Do not infer an operating international train from the physical railway to Georgia.

countries.name: Georgia
countries.note: Caucasus edition. Selected passenger corridors and published endpoints. Railway links across closed borders are excluded; published times require a current dated check.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.note: Transcontinental edition, shown for network context. Most of this network is in Asia. Selected trunk corridors are schematic; a current official first/last-stop inventory has not been imported, so no unverified pair is counted as a full train route. Full origin-to-final-station routes are pending verification; use the linked operator search.

countries.name: Andorra
countries.note: No railway inside Andorra. Rail access is via France or Spain followed by road transport; those transfers are not direct train routes.

countries.name: Monaco
countries.status: Rail service · no verified local origin
countries.note: Monaco–Monte-Carlo is served by SNCF regional trains. The mapped coastal corridor crosses borders; a stop in Monaco is not evidence that a train starts or finishes there. No independently verified Monaco-origin full route is currently listed.

countries.name: Liechtenstein
countries.status: Rail service · no verified local origin
countries.note: ÖBB regional trains use the Feldkirch–Buchs corridor through Liechtenstein. Schaan-Vaduz is an intermediate stop, not an assumed train terminus. The line reopened on 15 October 2026; verify the current timetable.

countries.name: San Marino

source.name: San Marino · official railway / transport reference

countries.note: No regular national passenger railway. Montale tunnel demonstration rides are heritage experiences and are excluded from the long-distance and regional mainline directory.

countries.name: Vatican City

source.name: Vatican City · official railway / transport reference

countries.note: Rail infrastructure exists, but no regular public mainline passenger timetable is included. Special excursions require separate confirmation. Roma San Pietro station is in Italy; it is not a Vatican-origin service.

countries.name: Malta
countries.note: No regular passenger railway. Public transport is by bus and ferry; historic railway remains are not current train routes.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.note: No regular passenger railway. The former Cyprus Government Railway closed in 1951; the railway museum is a heritage site, not a scheduled rail service.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.note: No public passenger railway. Bus, ferry and air connections are outside this railway directory.
